system.name: SkyPilot
system.one_liner: an intercloud broker that lets users run jobs across multiple cloud providers through a unified interface

components.name: Job specification (e.g., DAG)
components.role: user-provided task graph submitted to the broker

components.name: Intercloud Broker
components.role: central broker coordinating job placement and provisioning across clouds

components.name: Service Catalog
components.role: catalog of available cloud services, prices, and APIs across providers

components.name: Tracker
components.role: tracks state and availability of resources and services across clouds

components.name: Optimizer
components.role: selects a cloud/resource plan given the job spec and user preferences

components.name: Provisioner
components.role: provisions the chosen resources on the target cloud

components.name: Executor
components.role: executes the job on the provisioned resources

components.name: Service publisher
components.role: publishes a cloud's available services, APIs, and prices to the broker

components.name: Compatibility Set
components.role: set of compatible resources/services available on that cloud

components.name: Cloud A
components.role: one backend cloud provider the broker can provision on

components.name: Cloud B
components.role: another backend cloud provider the broker can provision on

flows.what: the user's task graph to be scheduled
APIs, prices, and other service information from the cloud
provisioned resources ready to run the job
provisioning requests sent to a cloud's compatible resources

content.key_idea: A single broker collects prices and API compatibility from many clouds into a catalog, then optimizes, provisions, and executes a user's job on whichever cloud fits their cost and latency preferences.
content.reading_order: Top to bottom: job specification and user preferences enter the Optimizer inside the Intercloud Broker box, which sits above two symmetric Cloud A / Cloud B backends it provisions into.

palette.used_for: dark slate blue for the Intercloud Broker outer box border/heading
pale blue fill for the Service Catalog/Tracker and Optimizer/Provisioner/Executor inner boxes
medium blue fill for the Compatibility Set boxes
gray fill for the Cloud A / Cloud B containers and Service publisher boxes

style.stroke: thin borders (~0.38pt), dashed outlines for the Cloud A/Cloud B containers
style.arrows: thin solid and dashed lines connecting the broker's components to each cloud's Service publisher, plus a plain arrow from the job-spec/user-preferences icon into the Optimizer
style.icons: a person icon for the job specification/user preferences input, small icons on the Service publisher boxes

encoding.color_means: darker blue marks the broker's own internal components (Service Catalog, Tracker, Optimizer, Provisioner, Executor); a distinct blue marks the per-cloud Compatibility Set boxes
encoding.line_style_means: dashed lines connect the broker to each cloud's Service publisher, suggesting a looser information exchange (prices, APIs) than the plain arrow carrying the job spec into the Optimizer
encoding.emphasis: the broker is drawn as one large box literally labelled Intercloud Broker straddling two symmetric Cloud A / Cloud B boxes below it, asserting that a single broker design generalizes across multiple, interchangeable cloud backends
reusable_patterns: central coordinator box stacked above N symmetric backend boxes
paired sub-components inside the coordinator (catalog/tracker vs optimizer/provisioner/executor) shown as two adjacent stacks
weaknesses: only two clouds are drawn, so it is not obvious from the figure alone whether the broker scales beyond two without reading the text

evidence: we propose an intercloud broker architecture consisting of the following components
Figure 3: Architecture of the intercloud broker.

summary: Figure 3 shows SkyPilot's intercloud broker architecture. A job specification (e.g., a DAG) and user preferences (e.g., minimize cost or latency) feed into the broker's Optimizer, which works alongside a Service Catalog and Tracker that record prices, APIs, and availability gathered from every backend cloud, and a Provisioner and Executor that carry out the chosen plan. Below the broker, two example backend clouds, Cloud A and Cloud B, each expose a Service publisher and a Compatibility Set describing the resources and services they offer; dashed connections carry this catalog information up to the broker, while the broker's Provisioner reaches back down to provision resources. The figure draws the broker as a single box stacked above symmetric per-cloud boxes, emphasizing that one broker design coordinates interchangeable cloud backends.
summary_zh: 图3展示SkyPilot跨云代理架构：作业规格与用户偏好输入Optimizer，配合Catalog/Tracker与Provisioner/Executor；Cloud A、B的Service publisher经虚线提供API、价格信息。
notes: layout-proposal: broker-over-backends — a single coordinator box (catalog/tracker plus optimizer/provisioner/executor) stacked above two symmetric, interchangeable cloud-backend panels, generalizing to N clouds rather than a radial hub with spokes arranged around it.
